from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Fetching storyboard data
        title = "The Hook: Same Point, Different Perspectives"
        lecture_lines = [
            "Alice uses a standard square coordinate grid.",
            "She sees a point at coordinates three-two.",
            "Bob uses a tilted and stretched coordinate grid.",
            "He sees the same point at coordinate one-one.",
            "Coordinates depend on the perspective you choose."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title, lecture_lines)
        
        # Basis Colors
        ALICE_GRID_COLOR = WHITE
        POINT_COLOR = RED
        BOB_GRID_COLOR = YELLOW
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Alice uses a standard square coordinate grid.
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(WHITE))
        
        # Create Alice's Grid
        alice_grid_lines = VGroup()
        for r in ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]:
            alice_grid_lines.add(Line(self.grid[f"{r}1"], self.grid[f"{r}6"], color=ALICE_GRID_COLOR, stroke_width=1, stroke_opacity=0.3))
        for c in ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]:
            alice_grid_lines.add(Line(self.grid[f"A{c}"], self.grid[f"F{c}"], color=ALICE_GRID_COLOR, stroke_width=1, stroke_opacity=0.3))
            
        self.play(Create(alice_grid_lines))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # She sees a point at coordinates three-two.
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(POINT_COLOR))
        
        # Alice's (3,2) point (from E2 origin)
        dot = Dot(color=POINT_COLOR, radius=0.1)
        self.place_at_grid(dot, "C5")
        
        # Label for Alice's view
        dot_label = Text("(3, 2)", font_size=20, color=WHITE)
        dot_label.next_to(dot, UR, buff=0.1)
        
        self.play(FadeIn(dot), Write(dot_label))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Bob uses a tilted and stretched coordinate grid.
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(BOB_GRID_COLOR))
        
        # Calculate Bob's Basis vectors using grid positions
        # Standard basis units: E2 to E3 (X), E2 to D2 (Y)
        O = self.grid["E2"]
        UX = self.grid["E3"] - O
        UY = self.grid["D2"] - O
        
        # Bob's basis (b1, b2) relative to Alice
        # Alice (3,2) -> Bob (1,1)
        # 1*b1 + 1*b2 = 3*UX + 2*UY
        # Let b1 = 2*UX + 1*UY, b2 = 1*UX + 1*UY
        b1 = 2 * UX + 1 * UY
        b2 = 1 * UX + 1 * UY
        
        bob_grid_lines = VGroup()
        # Generate Bob's grid lines: r = m*b1 + n*b2
        # Lines parallel to b1
        for n in range(-1, 5):
            line = Line(O + n*b2 - 2*b1, O + n*b2 + 3*b1, color=BOB_GRID_COLOR, stroke_width=2, stroke_opacity=0.6)
            bob_grid_lines.add(line)
        # Lines parallel to b2
        for m in range(-1, 5):
            line = Line(O + m*b1 - 2*b2, O + m*b1 + 4*b2, color=BOB_GRID_COLOR, stroke_width=2, stroke_opacity=0.6)
            bob_grid_lines.add(line)
            
        self.play(FadeOut(alice_grid_lines), FadeIn(bob_grid_lines))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        # He sees the same point at coordinate one-one.
        self.play(self.lecture[3].animate.set_color(BOB_GRID_COLOR))
        
        # Note: (1,1) in Bob's basis is 1*b1 + 1*b2 = (2+1, 1+1) = (3,2) in Alice's basis.
        # So the dot stays at the same screen position (C5).
        
        bob_label = Text("(1, 1)", font_size=20, color=BOB_GRID_COLOR)
        bob_label.move_to(dot_label.get_center())
        
        self.play(Transform(dot_label, bob_label))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        # Coordinates depend on the perspective you choose.
        self.play(self.lecture[4].animate.set_color(WHITE))
        
        # Final highlight of the point
        self.play(Flash(dot, color=WHITE, line_length=0.2, flash_radius=0.3))
        self.wait(2)

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # === Setup Layout ===
        title = "Prerequisite Check: What is a Basis?"
        lecture_lines = [
            "A basis is a set of spanning vectors.",
            "Standard unit vectors are i-hat and j-hat.",
            "Every vector is a recipe of basis vectors."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title, lecture_lines)
        
        # Colors
        COLOR_I = "#00FF00"  # Green
        COLOR_J = "#0000FF"  # Blue
        COLOR_V = "#FFFFFF"  # White
        COLOR_HIGHLIGHT = "#FFFF00"  # Yellow for active line highlighting

        # Origin point for the coordinate system
        origin = self.grid['D3']

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # "A basis is a set of spanning vectors."
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(COLOR_HIGHLIGHT))
        
        # Add visual context: a subtle grid on the right side
        grid_lines = VGroup()
        for r in ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]:
            grid_lines.add(Line(self.grid[f"{r}1"], self.grid[f"{r}6"], stroke_width=1, stroke_opacity=0.3, color=GRAY))
        for c in ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]:
            grid_lines.add(Line(self.grid[f"A{c}"], self.grid[f"F{c}"], stroke_width=1, stroke_opacity=0.3, color=GRAY))
        
        self.play(Create(grid_lines))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # "Standard unit vectors are i-hat and j-hat."
        self.play(
            self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(COLOR_HIGHLIGHT)
        )
        
        # i-hat (1, 0) -> from D3 to D4
        i_vec = Arrow(origin, self.grid['D4'], buff=0, color=COLOR_I, stroke_width=4)
        # Replaced MathTex with Text to avoid FileNotFoundError: 'latex'
        i_label = Text("i", slant=ITALIC, color=COLOR_I, font_size=24).next_to(i_vec, DOWN, buff=0.1)
        
        # j-hat (0, 1) -> from D3 to C3
        j_vec = Arrow(origin, self.grid['C3'], buff=0, color=COLOR_J, stroke_width=4)
        # Replaced MathTex with Text to avoid FileNotFoundError: 'latex'
        j_label = Text("j", slant=ITALIC, color=COLOR_J, font_size=24).next_to(j_vec, LEFT, buff=0.1)
        
        self.play(GrowArrow(i_vec), Write(i_label))
        self.play(GrowArrow(j_vec), Write(j_label))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # "Every vector is a recipe of basis vectors."
        self.play(
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(COLOR_HIGHLIGHT)
        )
        
        # Target vector v (3, 2) -> from D3 to B6
        v_vec = Arrow(origin, self.grid['B6'], buff=0, color=COLOR_V, stroke_width=5)
        # Replaced MathTex with Text to avoid FileNotFoundError: 'latex'
        v_label = Text("v", slant=ITALIC, color=COLOR_V, font_size=24).next_to(self.grid['B6'], UR, buff=0.1)
        
        self.play(Create(v_vec), Write(v_label))
        self.wait(1)
        
        # Step-by-step recipe: 3*i then 2*j
        i_steps = VGroup(
            Arrow(origin, self.grid['D4'], buff=0, color=COLOR_I, stroke_width=3),
            Arrow(self.grid['D4'], self.grid['D5'], buff=0, color=COLOR_I, stroke_width=3),
            Arrow(self.grid['D5'], self.grid['D6'], buff=0, color=COLOR_I, stroke_width=3)
        )
        
        j_steps = VGroup(
            Arrow(self.grid['D6'], self.grid['C6'], buff=0, color=COLOR_J, stroke_width=3),
            Arrow(self.grid['C6'], self.grid['B6'], buff=0, color=COLOR_J, stroke_width=3)
        )
        
        # Show the summation equation
        # Replaced MathTex with Text to avoid FileNotFoundError: 'latex'
        equation = Text("v = 3i + 2j", slant=ITALIC, color=WHITE, font_size=24)
        self.place_at_grid(equation, 'A5', scale_factor=1.0)
        
        # Animation sequence for the steps
        for step in i_steps:
            self.play(GrowArrow(step), run_time=0.5)
        for step in j_steps:
            self.play(GrowArrow(step), run_time=0.5)
            
        self.play(Write(equation))
        self.wait(2)

class TextMatrix(VGroup):
    """
    A custom Matrix replacement using Text brackets to avoid LaTeX dependencies.
    Mimics MobjectMatrix API for basic usage.
    """
    def __init__(self, mob_matrix, left_bracket="[", right_bracket="]"):
        super().__init__()
        self.mob_matrix = mob_matrix
        # Flatten entries for the elements VGroup
        self.elements = VGroup(*[mob for row in mob_matrix for mob in row])
        # Arrange in grid (rows, cols)
        self.elements.arrange_in_grid(rows=len(mob_matrix), cols=len(mob_matrix[0]), buff=(0.6, 0.4))
        self.add(self.elements)
        
        # Create brackets using Text instead of MathTex
        self.l_bracket = Text(left_bracket).scale(2)
        self.r_bracket = Text(right_bracket).scale(2)
        
        # Adjust height to fit the entries
        self.l_bracket.stretch_to_fit_height(self.elements.height + 0.3)
        self.r_bracket.stretch_to_fit_height(self.elements.height + 0.3)
        
        self.l_bracket.next_to(self.elements, LEFT, buff=0.15)
        self.r_bracket.next_to(self.elements, RIGHT, buff=0.15)
        
        self.add(self.l_bracket, self.r_bracket)

    def get_columns(self):
        """Returns a VGroup of VGroups, where each internal VGroup is a column of entries."""
        return VGroup(*[
            VGroup(*[self.mob_matrix[i][j] for i in range(len(self.mob_matrix))])
            for j in range(len(self.mob_matrix[0]))
        ])

    def get_brackets(self):
        """Returns the brackets as a VGroup."""
        return VGroup(self.l_bracket, self.r_bracket)

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # 1. Fetch info
        title = "Introducing the Transition Matrix"
        lines = [
            "We describe Bob's basis vectors using Alice's grid.",
            "These descriptions become the columns of transition matrix P.",
            "This matrix P translates between Bob and Alice."
        ]
        
        self.setup_layout(title, lines)
        
        # Define colors
        b1_color = "#FFFF00"  # Yellow
        b2_color = "#FF00FF"  # Magenta
        alice_color = BLUE_D
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        
        # Create Alice's grid (NumberPlane)
        alice_grid = NumberPlane(
            x_range=[-3, 3, 1],
            y_range=[-3, 3, 1],
            background_line_style={"stroke_color": alice_color, "stroke_opacity": 0.4},
            axis_config={"stroke_color": alice_color},
            x_length=4,
            y_length=4
        )
        self.place_in_area(alice_grid, "B1", "E4", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        # Create Bob's basis vectors
        b1_vec = Arrow(alice_grid.c2p(0, 0), alice_grid.c2p(2, 1), buff=0, color=b1_color, stroke_width=4)
        b2_vec = Arrow(alice_grid.c2p(0, 0), alice_grid.c2p(-1, 1), buff=0, color=b2_color, stroke_width=4)
        
        b1_label = Text("b1", color=b1_color, font_size=24, slant=ITALIC)
        b2_label = Text("b2", color=b2_color, font_size=24, slant=ITALIC)
        
        b1_label.next_to(b1_vec.get_end(), UR, buff=0.1)
        b2_label.next_to(b2_vec.get_end(), UL, buff=0.1)
        
        self.play(Create(alice_grid))
        self.play(GrowArrow(b1_vec), Write(b1_label))
        self.play(GrowArrow(b2_vec), Write(b2_label))
        self.wait(1)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(
            self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(YELLOW)
        )
        
        # Create matrix P using custom TextMatrix
        m_entries = [
            [Text("2", color=b1_color, font_size=32), Text("-1", color=b2_color, font_size=32)],
            [Text("1", color=b1_color, font_size=32), Text("1", color=b2_color, font_size=32)]
        ]
        matrix_p = TextMatrix(m_entries, left_bracket="[", right_bracket="]")
        p_label = Text("P =", font_size=32, color=WHITE).next_to(matrix_p, LEFT)
        matrix_group = VGroup(p_label, matrix_p)
        self.place_at_grid(matrix_group, "C5", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        # Show coordinate vectors using TextMatrix
        b1_coords = TextMatrix(
            [[Text("2", font_size=24)], [Text("1", font_size=24)]],
            left_bracket="[", right_bracket="]"
        ).set_color(b1_color).scale(0.8)
        
        b2_coords = TextMatrix(
            [[Text("-1", font_size=24)], [Text("1", font_size=24)]],
            left_bracket="[", right_bracket="]"
        ).set_color(b2_color).scale(0.8)
        
        b1_coords.next_to(b1_vec.get_end(), DR, buff=0.2)
        b2_coords.next_to(b2_vec.get_end(), DL, buff=0.2)
        
        self.play(Write(b1_coords))
        self.play(Write(b2_coords))
        self.wait(0.5)
        
        # Reveal Matrix skeleton
        self.play(
            FadeIn(p_label),
            FadeIn(matrix_p.get_brackets())
        )
        
        # Animate coordinates into matrix columns
        self.play(
            ReplacementTransform(b1_coords, matrix_p.get_columns()[0]),
            ReplacementTransform(b2_coords, matrix_p.get_columns()[1]),
            run_time=2
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(YELLOW)
        )
        
        col1 = matrix_p.get_columns()[0]
        col2 = matrix_p.get_columns()[1]
        
        self.play(
            Flash(b1_vec, color=b1_color, line_length=0.3),
            Flash(col1, color=b1_color, line_length=0.3)
        )
        self.wait(0.5)
        self.play(
            Flash(b2_vec, color=b2_color, line_length=0.3),
            Flash(col2, color=b2_color, line_length=0.3)
        )
        
        self.wait(2)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Define lecture lines with bullets as per instruction
        lecture_lines = [
            "- Bob's coordinates are transformed using this matrix formula.",
            "- We start with Bob's coordinate point at one-one.",
            "- Multiplying by P warps Bob's grid into Alice's.",
            "- The calculation results in Alice's coordinates one-two.",
            "- The point now matches Alice's standard grid perspective."
        ]
        
        self.setup_layout("The Transformation Formula", lecture_lines)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Bob's coordinates are transformed using this matrix formula.
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        
        # Formula: v_std = P * v_alt
        # Replaced MathTex with VGroup of Text to avoid FileNotFoundError: 'latex'
        formula = VGroup(
            Text("v_std", font_size=32),
            Text("=", font_size=32),
            Text("P", font_size=32),
            Text("v_alt", font_size=32)
        ).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.2).set_color(WHITE)
        
        # Place formula in the top area of the right side (A1 to B6)
        self.place_in_area(formula, "A1", "B6", scale_factor=1.1)
        self.play(Write(formula))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # We start with Bob's coordinate point at one-one.
        self.play(
            self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(YELLOW)
        )
        
        # Bob's yellow grid (tilted)
        matrix = [[2, -1], [1, 1]]
        bob_grid = NumberPlane(
            x_range=[-4, 4, 1],
            y_range=[-4, 4, 1],
            background_line_style={"stroke_color": YELLOW, "stroke_opacity": 0.5},
            axis_config={"stroke_color": YELLOW, "stroke_width": 2}
        )
        bob_grid.apply_matrix(matrix)
        # Place grid in the lower area of the right side (C1 to F6)
        self.place_in_area(bob_grid, "C1", "F6", scale_factor=0.6)
        
        # Point at (1,1) in Bob's basis

class Section6Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Setup title and lecture lines
        title_str = "Summary & Real-World Intuition"
        lecture_lines = [
            "Change of basis simplifies many complex mathematical problems.",
            "It's like switching languages to describe the same world.",
            "Choosing the right basis reveals hidden structures."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title_str, lecture_lines)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Show a 4x4 grid of gray squares (#888888) representing pixels.
        self.lecture[0].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        pixel_grid = VGroup()
        for r in range(4):
            for c in range(4):
                square = Square(side_length=0.4, fill_opacity=1, fill_color="#888888", stroke_width=1, stroke_color=WHITE)
                # Map r,c to grid positions B2 to E5 roughly
                row_char = chr(ord('B') + r)
                col_char = str(2 + c)
                self.place_at_grid(square, f"{row_char}{col_char}")
                pixel_grid.add(square)
        
        self.play(FadeIn(pixel_grid))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Morph the squares into 4 different colored wave patterns (#00FFFF, #FF00FF, #FFFF00, #00FF00).
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        colors = ["#00FFFF", "#FF00FF", "#FFFF00", "#00FF00"]
        waves = VGroup()
        
        for i in range(4):
            # Create a wave for each color. Using Sine wave as the pattern.
            wave = FunctionGraph(
                lambda x: 0.3 * np.sin(2 * PI * x + i * PI/2),
                x_range=[-1, 1],
                color=colors[i]
            )
            # Position each wave in one of the rows of the area
            row_char = chr(ord('B') + i)
            self.place_in_area(wave, f"{row_char}2", f"{row_char}5")
            waves.add(wave)

        # Split pixel_grid into 4 groups for morphing
        grid_groups = [pixel_grid[i*4:(i+1)*4] for i in range(4)]
        
        self.play(
            *[ReplacementTransform(grid_groups[i], waves[i]) for i in range(4)],
            run_time=2
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Fade in text "Simpler Representation" in white (#FFFFFF).
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        simpler_text = Text("Simpler Representation", font_size=24, color="#FFFFFF")
        # Place text below the waves
        self.place_in_area(simpler_text, "F2", "F5")
        
        self.play(FadeIn(simpler_text))
        self.wait(2)

        # Final cleanup/end state
        self.lecture[2].set_color(WHITE)
        self.wait(1)

outline.topic: Change of Basis: A Tale of Two Grids

sections.title: The Hook: Same Point, Different Perspectives
sections.content: Introduce two characters, Alice and Bob, looking at the same point in space. Alice uses a standard square grid (Standard Basis), while Bob uses a tilted, stretched grid (Alternative Basis). Explain that while the point doesn't move, the numbers used to describe its location change based on the 'language' (basis) being spoken.
sections.example: A cat sits at a specific spot. Alice says the cat is at (3, 2). Bob, standing on a tilted hill, says the cat is at (1, 1) according to his coordinates.

sections.title: Prerequisite Check: What is a Basis?
sections.content: Briefly review that a basis is a set of linearly independent vectors that 'span' the space. Visually show the standard unit vectors i (1, 0) and j (0, 1). Explain that any vector is just a 'recipe' of these basis vectors.
sections.example: Visualizing the vector [3, 2] as 3 steps of vector 'i' and 2 steps of vector 'j' on a Cartesian plane.

sections.title: Introducing the Transition Matrix
sections.content: Define the Change of Basis Matrix (P). Explain that to speak Bob's language, we need to know what Bob's basis vectors look like from Alice's perspective. These 'foreign' vectors become the columns of our transition matrix.
sections.example: If Bob's first basis vector b1 is [2, 1] and his second b2 is [-1, 1] in Alice's system, the matrix P = [[2, -1], [1, 1]].

sections.title: The Transformation Formula
sections.content: Present the core formula: v_standard = P * v_alternate. Show graphically how multiplying Bob's coordinates by matrix P 'warps' his grid back into Alice's standard grid. Emphasize that P maps Bob's coordinates to Alice's coordinates.
sections.example: Using Bob's coordinate [1, 1], we calculate P * [1, 1] = [2-1, 1+1] = [1, 2]. Visually show the point landing in the correct spot on Alice's grid.

sections.title: The Inverse: Returning to the Alternate Basis
sections.content: Explain how to go the other way. If we have Alice's coordinates and want Bob's, we use the inverse matrix (P⁻¹). v_alternate = P⁻¹ * v_standard.
sections.example: An animation showing Alice's square grid 'squishing' and 'tilting' to match Bob's skewed perspective through the application of the inverse matrix.

sections.title: Summary & Real-World Intuition
sections.content: Summarize that a change of basis is simply a coordinate transformation. Mention why we do this: some problems (like diagonalizing matrices or image compression) are much easier to solve in a 'custom' basis than the standard one.
sections.example: A JPEG image compressor 'changing basis' from pixels to frequency components to save space, much like Bob choosing a basis that aligns with the slope of his hill.
